Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 78 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO, Aurea), Liam O'Connor (SRE, Aurea), Sara Gomez (Security, Aurea), Diego Ruiz (Infra Eng, Aurea)

Auto-generated summary (may omit details): Deep lab on private VPC topology and runtime perf.

Topics: PrivateLink, NAT hairpin, DNS resolver, KV cache, batching windows, quantization, p99 latency

---- Transcript ----
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um i'm maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. quick roll call?
[00:07] Priya Nair: yeah this is priya, i'll kick off and we'll try to keep it technical. thanks for scheduling.
[00:12] Ethan Park: hey priya, maya, liam, sara, diego — ethan here, i'll drive the deep dive on runtime and networking.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: liam — we've got our staging cluster and a VPN back to the private network, happy to walk through current topology.
[00:24] Maya Chen: great. rough agenda — first 20 we'll map network, next 30 runtime perf and caching, last 20 ops and next steps. sound ok?
[00:31] Priya Nair: perfect.
[00:35] Diego Ruiz: quick note: we've seen occasional tail latency spikes when traffic routes via our NAT, curious if that's hairpin related.
[00:43] Ethan Park: yep that's one hypothesis. before we dig in: what are your SLOs — p95/p99?
[00:49] Sara Gomez: security ask first: we need audit logs, KMS for encryption, and SAML SSO — we'll need the SOC2 pack.
[00:56] Maya Chen: we'll share SOC2 and KMS integration notes after, i put that in action items.
[01:02] Priya Nair: our target is p95 < 120ms for chat completions at 50-100 qps, p99 ideally < 300ms but we can accept some tradeoffs for throughput.
[01:12] Ethan Park: good to know. how big are your payloads? typical prompt lengths?
[01:16] Liam O'Connor: average context is 512 tokens, up to 2k in some flows. embeddings are separate but lower priority.
[01:23] Ethan Park: that impacts KV cache hit rate — kv cache warms better with shorter prefixes and steady session affinity. are you using session-level pinning?
[01:31] Diego Ruiz: we currently don't pin, tokens come from multiple microservices so affinity is loose.
[01:36] Ethan Park: ok. with loose affinity you'll see more cold-cache decoding and higher p99 — two levers: 1) prefix KV caching with sticky routing, 2) larger hot-shard memory to reduce eviction.
[01:49] Priya Nair: we prefer not to change client-side too much — any server-side knobs?
[01:54] Ethan Park: yes, on the Redwood runtime we can adjust KV eviction thresholds, increase local in-memory stripe size, and employ predictive prefetch for known conversation IDs. that increases memory but reduces cold token cost.
[02:05] Liam O'Connor: memory is fine, cpu isn't our limiter. the concern is network path — sometimes traffic goes out to our NAT and comes back (hairpin) through the same NAT GW which spikes RTT.
[02:16] Ethan Park: hairpinning can add 20-200ms depending on provider and routes. PrivateLink avoids hairpin by creating a cross-account endpoint that stays inside provider backbone. you lose some flexibility but you cut that RTT.
[02:30] Sara Gomez: how does PrivateLink affect egress controls and logging? we need flow logs and auditability.
[02:36] Maya Chen: PrivateLink still emits VPC flow logs and we can enable ENI-level tracing in our setup. we'll also push logs to your splunk/elk via forwarder or S3.
[02:45] Priya Nair: what about MTU and fragmentation? we have IPSec tunnels to a colo and noticed truncation/slowdowns on larger payloads.
[02:53] Ethan Park: good call — MTU mismatch leads to fragmentation which can blow up latency at p99. we usually recommend path MTU discovery and set the ENI MTU to 9001 where possible, and lower the application payload chunking so attention windows stream smaller frames.
[03:07] Diego Ruiz: our VPN only supports 1500, we can't change that easily. any mitigation?
[03:11] Ethan Park: you can enable tcp MSS clamping on the VPN and adjust maximum chunk size for RPC calls to avoid fragmentation. also consider stitching via PrivateLink on the cloud side to reduce hops across the VPN for inference traffic.
[03:23] Liam O'Connor: about DNS — split-horizon DNS is in play: internal names resolve differently over the VPN and over the clouds. we've seen intermittent failures when resolvers fall back.
[03:34] Ethan Park: resolvers are critical. best practice: configure dedicated inbound/resolver endpoints in the VPC for Redwood Private so calls to model registry and CRLs resolve locally. add a low TTL for debug but increase TTL on stable entries after cutover.
[03:46] Priya Nair: ok. on the Redwood side — does the runtime require outbound internet for model fetching or telemetry? we need to ensure no egress to public internet for compliance.
[03:57] Maya Chen: we support fully private mode — model artifacts can be preloaded via S3 private endpoints or an on-prem artifact mirror. telemetry can be routed over your egress proxies or disabled; we'll send logs to a customer-owned S3 if required.
[04:11] Sara Gomez: KMS integration?
[04:13] Maya Chen: yes — we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS or HSM) for key wrapping; config for rotating keys is documented. i'll attach the security pack after the call.
[04:22] Ethan Park: shifting to runtime perf — small primer: quantization (8-bit/4-bit) reduces memory and improves throughput but sometimes increases token generation variance which can affect p99. our tests show 4-bit gains on throughput but p99 can move from 300ms to 420ms in contrived tails if not tuned.
[04:41] Liam O'Connor: that's significant. do we have hybrid options? like quantize tail but keep core fp16?
[04:47] Ethan Park: yes — model slicing and mixed-precision layers are options; we can keep attention matrices in fp16 and quantize feed-forward layers, or run a fallback to fp16 for slow requests. this increases complexity but often gets the best of both worlds.
[05:01] Diego Ruiz: how do batching windows interact? we saw increased latency when batching aggressively at lower qps.
[05:08] Ethan Park: dynamic batching heuristics: set a max batch size and a wait threshold (e.g., 5ms). at low qps, prefer micro-batching or disable batching for latency-sensitive flows. at high qps, batching improves throughput significantly. Redwood's profiler recommends per-route policies — we can auto-suggest thresholds based on traffic shape.
[05:24] Priya Nair: can we test different thresholds without redeploying?
[05:28] Ethan Park: yes, tuning is runtime-configurable via the console or API — no model push needed. we can stage changes in canary and roll out.
[05:35] Maya Chen: quick checkpoint — sounds like action items around network topology and a pilot. anyone object?
[05:40] Priya Nair: go ahead.
[05:42] Liam O'Connor: one more network nuance — cross-account PrivateLink needs an accept step on our side; also the endpoint ENI consumes IPs in the subnet so we need to reserve addresses.
[05:52] Ethan Park: good catch — we'll provide terraform snippets and call out subnet sizing. common mistake is placing the endpoint in a small private subnet and then running out of IPs during scale tests.
[06:04] Diego Ruiz: speaking of scale, for dedicated capacity do you allow bursting to hosted cluster in emergencies?
[06:10] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Dedicated has burst-to-hosted policy configurable per customer; there's a routing policy and fallback model variants to keep availability while respecting data isolation constraints. we'll flag this in pilot docs.
[06:21] Sara Gomez: legal — needed: DPA and details on data residency. we'll take that in the security package.
[06:27] Maya Chen: got it. i'll attach DPA and regional hosting options.
[06:31] Ethan Park: going back to KV cache — we recommend hot-sharding by conversation hash and a 5k entry hot window for customer chat workloads. that plus sticky routing reduces token-level fill rate by ~40% in our benchmark.
[06:44] Priya Nair: if we shard by conversation id, what's the impact on autoscaling? could one shard hot-spot a GPU?
[06:51] Ethan Park: possibility exists. mitigation is to use consistent hashing with bounded loads and spillover queues; Redwood's orchestrator can detect a hot-shard and replicate cache state to a warm neighbor to spread load. there is a short window where latency may spike while replication converges.
[07:05] Liam O'Connor: replication could be heavy on network traffic — will that saturate our inter-AZ links?
[07:12] Ethan Park: replication is prioritized and batched; on heavy churn we recommend placing hot-shards in the same AZ to keep replication intra-AZ. we'll also provide a bandwidth budget estimate.
[07:24] Diego Ruiz: benchmarking: what exact tests should we run for the pilot?
[07:28] Maya Chen: proposal: 1) baseline p50/p95/p99 at 50qps and 200qps with fp16 model and no batching; 2) repeat with quantized model (4-bit) and tuned batching; 3) run hairpin scenario by routing through NAT and measure delta; 4) run PrivateLink path and compare. we'll provide the harness and expected payload shapes.
[07:45] Priya Nair: timeline?
[07:47] Maya Chen: start pilot week of 2026-11-08 for two weeks.
[07:50] Sara Gomez: that works.
[07:52] Ethan Park: quick note on observability — we'll surface token-level cost and latency in the console and provide tracing hooks to tie model calls back to request IDs. that should help debug p99 by peeling the onion: network vs runtime vs model.
[08:04] Priya Nair: can you show an example trace?
[08:06] Ethan Park: i'll attach a screenshot and a sample trace link, but brief: trace shows DNS lookup, TCP connect, L7 handshake, request enqueue, KV cache hit/miss, decode token latencies — all timestamped at millisecond resolution.
[08:20] Diego Ruiz: any gotchas with egress proxies? we have a corporate proxy requiring TLS inspection.
[08:26] Ethan Park: TLS inspection can break HTTP/2 keepalive and increase cpu on sidecars; if possible, allow passthrough for inference endpoints or configure the proxy for long-lived connections. also ensure SNI and ALPN are preserved.
[08:40] Liam O'Connor: about private artifact sync — we'll mirror models on S3; what's the best way to seed the runtime without causing cold starts?
[08:47] Ethan Park: prewarm instances and preload KV caches for top N models at deploy time; Redwood can orchestrate a staged rollout that warms the cache by replaying representative prompts from a scrubbed dataset.
[08:59] Priya Nair: that sounds helpful. do you need sample datasets?
[09:02] Maya Chen: yes — if you can provide an anonymized prompt set we can run prewarm scripts.
[09:08] Sara Gomez: compliance question: will prewarm logs contain PII? we need to ensure scrubbers run prior.
[09:14] Ethan Park: we have built-in scrubbers; we'll show the config in the security pack.
[09:19] Maya Chen: final recap and next steps — we will: share security pack (SOC2, DPA, KMS notes), share terraform snippets and PrivateLink accept flow, send runtime tuning doc and sample kernel flags, provision a temp PrivateLink endpoint for pilot, and schedule the network runbook workshop for 2026-11-10.
[09:36] Priya Nair: ok thanks, action items look good.
[09:40] Liam O'Connor: thanks team.
[09:42] Diego Ruiz: one last thing — please call out IP reservation numbers for ENI and plan for scale tests.
[09:48] Ethan Park: will do.
[09:50] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invites.
[09:55] (call ends, recording stopped)

Notes: references to shared artifacts: "pilot-harness.csv" (benchmark payloads), "redwood-privatelink-terraform.md" (snippet), security pack link (sent post-call).
